findings.issue: The hero photo still carries the 30-word lead ('Since 2011 we have run bulk lines…'), centred in four lines under the two-line title, and the aqua CONTACT US pill below it, although the site rule says a lead much longer than the competitor's stands under the hero.
findings.reference: The competitor's About hero is the factory photo with only the centred white H1 (Maison 700 45px) on it: no lead and no button (section-modules: 'no lead, no CTA').
findings.fix: Give PageHero.astro's on-photo lead limit (heroLeadShown(), heroText.leadWords) a value per page type, with 0 words for the about reference, so the about lead and its button go into the block under the hero and only the H1 stays on the photo.

findings.issue: On phones the same lead runs to four lines of small centred text over the busy wall-and-roses photo, between the three-line title and the large aqua pill, so the lower half of the hero is all text over the picture.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero carries only the white H1 over its photo, and its text starts under the photo.
findings.fix: Use the same per-page-type lead limit in PageHero.astro (heroLeadShown()), so at every width the about lead and its button stand under the hero.

findings.issue: On phones the single quote card in view still has a blank band about 80px tall between the five-line quote and its rule: the subgrid levelling in reference.css (lines 506–509) is still unconditional, so the quote track takes the height of the hidden second card's longer quote.
findings.reference: The competitor's quote cards put the attribution straight under the quote, with no empty band.
findings.fix: In reference.css, apply the four `.testimonials[data-variant="carousel"]:not(:has(.testimonial__headline))` subgrid rules only when the cards share a row (wrap them in @media (min-width: 768px), or scope them to `.track[data-fits]`), so a phone card sizes to its own quote.

findings.issue: On /about-us/ the 'About Us' nav item still looks the same as the other items: no nav link gets aria-current, so the treatment's `.site-nav__link[aria-current="page"]` underline never applies.
findings.reference: The competitor's header shows the current page's item ('About') in a lighter tone.
findings.fix: In SiteHeader.astro, set aria-current="page" on the nav link (and on the dropdown sublink) whose route matches the current page.

findings.issue: The tall phone frame still crops the photo down to the stone wall and roses: the sitter shows only as part of a dress at the lower-right edge, under the button.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero uses its own phone crop (banner-about-us-mobile.webp), so the scene stays inside the frame.
findings.fix: Have the template give the about hero photo a phone crop, or centre it on the sitter (a judged focal point set by the template, not by reference.css).

findings.issue: Two of the four figures still read as cut-off phrases ('65 that' over 'SAMPLING TEAM', '55 custom' over 'DAILY SAMPLES'). On phones '100,000 pieces' wraps to two lines, so 'MONTHLY CAPACITY' sits lower than 'FOUNDED' beside it.
findings.reference: The competitor's figure rows set a short value over a clear uppercase label.
findings.fix: Site Factory: rewrite the value/label pairs, e.g. '65' / 'person sampling team', '55' / 'custom samples a day', '100,000' / 'pieces a month'.

findings.issue: The six steps wrap into two rows of three, but the connecting line still runs only through markers 01–03 and on past 03 to the column edge, while 04–06 have no line, so the second row looks cut off from the sequence.
findings.reference: The competitor's step module sets every step on the same hairline.
findings.fix: Draw the process rule (`.process-steps::before`) once per row, on that row's marker line, and end it at the row's last marker, not as one line across the whole list.

findings.issue: After m6's tint, the logo row, the testimonials and the FAQ still stand on white one after another (the same at 390px), while every section above them alternates.
findings.reference: The site rule: neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds, set by the template.
findings.fix: Make the template's section-surface alternation count the logos and testimonials blocks, so the testimonials section takes --section-tint and breaks up the white run (its cards then take the white card fill).

findings.issue: m5 ('How We Check Quality at Every Stage') and m6 ('Certifications and Compliance Paperwork') are still both a heading with a check list beside it, one under the other. Only the background tells them apart, and m5's heading column stands empty for about 300px under its two lines.
findings.reference: The site rule: two sections of the same shape do not stand one under the other; the template sets only one of them out as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: In the template's layout pass, when two neighbouring iconList sections both have the list-beside-heading shape, set the second one out differently (e.g. a two-column check grid under its heading).

findings.issue: The second question still breaks at the hyphen of 'in-house' ('…pattern makers in-' / 'house to develop our styles?'), so the heading reads as a word split across two lines.
findings.reference: The competitor's questions keep their words whole on a line.
findings.fix: Site Factory: write 'in‑house' with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011) in this FAQ question, or reword it (e.g. 'in your own studio'), so the compound stays on one line.

findings.issue: 'Brands we make for' and the next section's 'What buyers say' are in sentence case, while every other section heading on the page is in Title Case ('The Brands We Work With Directly', 'Frequently Asked Questions'), so these two headings look like they come from another page.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one capitalisation for all its section headings.
findings.fix: Site Factory / site-proof.json: write the owner-logos and owner-testimonials headings in Title Case ('Brands We Make For', 'What Buyers Say').
